Instead, it states:

  • Enrollment was open.
  • Course content for enrolled trainees was scheduled to become available from May 12, 2025.
  • No separate closing date for applications was provided.

Since the stated course-access date is from a previous edition, applicants should check the official World Bank course platform for the latest enrollment information and any new deadline.

How to Enroll

Interested participants can begin by visiting the World Bank Institute’s online course platform.

The general process involves:

  1. Visit the official World Bank Institute course platform.
  2. Locate the Introduction to Behavioral Science in Public Policy course.
  3. Review the current course information and enrollment status.
  4. Create an account or sign in if required.
  5. Enroll in the course.
  6. Complete the required pre-course assessment.
  7. Work through the video lessons, readings, activities, and case studies.
  8. Participate in the required discussion activities.
  9. Complete the knowledge checks.
  10. Complete the mandatory post-course assessment.
  11. Follow the course requirements for receiving the certificate.

Applicants should always follow the instructions displayed on the current official course page because course schedules and enrollment procedures can change between editions.

Enroll Now

Why Learn Behavioral Science?

Behavioral science provides a useful perspective for understanding the gap between how policies are designed and how people actually respond to them.

Traditional policy approaches may focus heavily on economic incentives, regulations, resources, or information. Behavioral science adds another layer by asking questions such as:

  • How do people actually make decisions?
  • What happens when people are under pressure?
  • How do social expectations influence behavior?
  • Why do people sometimes behave differently from what policymakers expect?
  • How do existing beliefs influence decisions?
  • How can programs be designed around real human behavior?
  • How can behavioral insights improve policy outcomes?

These questions are particularly important in international development, where policies and programs operate across diverse social, economic, and cultural environments.

Benefits of Taking the Course

Participants can potentially gain several benefits from completing the training.

Develop Knowledge of Behavioral Science

The course provides an introduction to important behavioral science concepts and terminology.

Understand Human Decision-Making

Participants explore automatic thinking, social thinking, and mental models and how these processes influence decisions.

Connect Theory With Real-World Policy

Case studies help demonstrate how behavioral science can be applied to actual development and policy challenges.

Strengthen Public Policy Knowledge

The course can complement existing knowledge in public policy, economics, development studies, public administration, and related disciplines.

Learn From World Bank Approaches

Participants are introduced to behavioral science methodologies associated with the World Bank’s work in international development.

Gain an Online Certificate

Participants who meet the course requirements can receive a certificate of completion.

Study Flexibly Online

Because the training is delivered through an e-learning platform, participants can study remotely rather than attending a physical training location.

Final Thoughts

The Introduction to Behavioral Science in Public Policy: New Edition provides an introduction to an increasingly important area of public policy and international development.

Rather than looking only at policies, regulations, incentives, or resources, behavioral science considers the people who ultimately interact with and respond to those policies. The course introduces participants to three major ways of understanding human thinking: automatic thinking, social thinking, and thinking through mental models.

Through videos, readings, interactive games, case studies, discussion forums, assessments, and practical examples, participants can explore how behavioral insights may be applied to areas such as education, healthcare, taxation, gender equality, social norms, and climate change.

The course is particularly relevant to policy practitioners and researchers interested in applying behavioral science to development-related public policy, while people studying or working in international development, economics, public administration, social sciences, and related fields may also find the subject valuable.

The training is approximately 6 hours long, delivered online, and includes a certificate upon successful completion of the required activities.

However, prospective applicants should pay close attention to the course’s current status. The supplied information refers to content becoming available from May 12, 2025, and does not state a final application deadline. Since that date has passed, applicants should visit the official World Bank Institute course platform to determine whether a new edition is currently available and to confirm the latest enrollment dates and requirements.

Stay updated with new World Bank courses, learning opportunities, and future editions by subscribing to the official newsletter.

The Westerwelle Foundation for International Understanding is inviting eligible national service candidates to apply for three National Service positions at the Westerwelle Startup Haus Accra (WSHAC) in Accra, Ghana. The available positions are Operations & Admin Assistant, Programs Assistant, and Community & Marketing Assistant.

These opportunities provide an opportunity for young professionals to gain practical experience within an international entrepreneurship and innovation ecosystem while contributing to the development of one of Ghana’s newest startup hubs.

Application Deadline: Applications are accepted on a rolling basis.

About the Westerwelle Foundation

The Westerwelle Foundation for International Understanding is a non-profit organization headquartered in Berlin, Germany. The Foundation was established in 2013 by Dr. Guido Westerwelle, former German Minister for Foreign Affairs, and Ralph Dommermuth, CEO and Founder of United Internet AG.

The Foundation focuses on accelerating digital transformation in emerging economies and supporting positive developments that contribute to transparency, integrity, innovation, entrepreneurship, and stronger institutions.

One of the Foundation’s key initiatives is the Westerwelle Startup Haus, a network of entrepreneurship hubs designed to support entrepreneurs, innovators, and emerging businesses through access to workspaces, networks, mentoring, entrepreneurship programmes, and other forms of ecosystem support.

The Westerwelle Startup Haus network includes locations in:

  • Tunis, Tunisia
  • Kigali, Rwanda
  • Arusha, Tanzania
  • Mombasa, Kenya
  • Accra, Ghana

Through these hubs, the Foundation seeks to strengthen entrepreneurship ecosystems and facilitate collaboration between founders, investors, corporations, universities, development organizations, and other ecosystem partners.

About Westerwelle Startup Haus Accra

The Westerwelle Startup Haus Accra is based in Accra, Ghana, and is being developed as a collaborative entrepreneurship and innovation hub.

The hub brings together a wide range of stakeholders, including:

  • Startup founders
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Innovators
  • Investors
  • Corporates
  • Universities
  • Mentors
  • Facilitators
  • Ecosystem partners

WSHAC provides flexible workspaces, entrepreneurship programmes, networking opportunities, and strategic partnerships intended to help entrepreneurs build and grow scalable businesses.

The Accra hub also aims to contribute to Ghana’s broader innovation ecosystem by creating opportunities for collaboration and knowledge exchange across Ghana, Africa, and international markets.

For national service candidates, working at WSHAC provides exposure to an environment where entrepreneurship, innovation, communications, programme delivery, administration, community engagement, and business support intersect.

Available Westerwelle Startup Haus Accra National Service Positions

There are currently three National Service opportunities available at Westerwelle Startup Haus Accra.

1. National Service Position: Operations & Admin Assistant

Location: Accra, Ghana

Application Deadline: Rolling basis

The Operations & Admin Assistant will support the day-to-day running of the Westerwelle Startup Haus Accra while also assisting with finance and administrative functions.

The position is particularly suited to candidates who are organized, detail-oriented, reliable, comfortable working with documentation, and interested in administration, finance, logistics, procurement, or office operations.

Key Responsibilities

The successful candidate will support several areas of the Haus’s daily operations.

Facilities and Office Operations

Responsibilities will include:

  • Logging maintenance issues involving electricity, internet connectivity, air conditioning, printers, furniture, and other office facilities.
  • Following up with service providers until maintenance and operational issues are fully resolved.
  • Monitoring stock levels for stationery, printing materials, kitchen supplies, and cleaning products.
  • Raising supply requests before essential items run out.
  • Supporting room setup and resetting rooms following meetings, training sessions, programmes, and events.
  • Maintaining the office inventory.
  • Maintaining the fixed asset register.

The role therefore requires someone who can identify operational problems, follow up consistently, and ensure that outstanding issues are not left unresolved.

Documentation and Filing

The Operations & Admin Assistant will also be responsible for supporting accurate and organized documentation.

Duties include:

  • Collecting and filing supplier invoices.
  • Organizing contracts and delivery notes.
  • Maintaining tax certificates and receipts.
  • Maintaining the digital filing structure in SharePoint.
  • Maintaining supplier records in Airtable.
  • Following established document naming conventions.
  • Scanning and indexing physical documents.
  • Keeping finance-related files organized and audit-ready throughout the year.

Attention to detail and confidentiality are particularly important because the position involves financial and commercial documentation.

Procurement Support

The position also provides exposure to procurement-related activities.

The successful candidate will:

  • Request supplier quotations when instructed.
  • Compile quotations for evaluation.
  • Maintain the supplier database.
  • Keep supplier registration information up to date.
  • Track VAT and tax clearance documentation.
  • Track deliveries against purchase orders.
  • Confirm that ordered goods have been received.

Finance Support

The Operations & Admin Assistant will work under supervision to support basic finance processes.

Responsibilities include:

  • Assisting with transaction entry into the accounting system.
  • Supporting preparation of the monthly document pack for the accountant.
  • Following up on outstanding member and client invoices.

Candidates should therefore be comfortable working with numbers, records, spreadsheets, and confidential information.

General Administration

The role will also involve supporting travel and logistics arrangements, including:

  • Travel bookings
  • Accommodation arrangements
  • Logistics for staff
  • Logistics for facilitators
  • Logistics for guests

Qualifications and Experience

Applicants for the Operations & Admin Assistant position should have:

  • A Bachelor’s degree or HND in accounting, finance, business administration, logistics, or a related discipline.
  • Eligibility for the 2026/2027 national service cycle.
  • Strong Excel skills.
  • Willingness to learn QuickBooks or the accounting system selected by WSHAC.
  • A practical and persistent approach to dealing with service providers.
  • The ability to follow issues through to resolution.
  • Strong discretion when handling confidential financial and commercial information.
  • Demonstrable integrity and reliability.
  • References supporting the applicant’s integrity and reliability.

APPLY HERE

2. National Service Position: Programs Assistant

Location: Accra, Ghana

Application Deadline: Rolling basis

The Programs Assistant will support the delivery of Westerwelle Startup Haus Accra’s programme calendar.

The role includes supporting programme outreach, participant coordination, session logistics, data management, reporting, community follow-up, and engagement with mentors, facilitators, experts, and startup founders.

The position may be particularly relevant to candidates with backgrounds in business, economics, development studies, social sciences, communications, or related disciplines who have an interest in entrepreneurship and Ghana’s startup ecosystem.

Key Responsibilities

Programme Delivery

The Programs Assistant will help ensure that programmes and sessions are delivered efficiently and according to schedule.

Responsibilities include:

  • Supporting outreach activities.
  • Publishing programme calls.
  • Responding to applicant enquiries.
  • Compiling applications for review.
  • Maintaining participant lists.
  • Maintaining participant contact records.
  • Maintaining attendance logs.
  • Preparing session materials.
  • Preparing name badges.
  • Preparing handouts.
  • Preparing feedback forms.
  • Coordinating room setup.
  • Coordinating equipment requirements.
  • Coordinating refreshments with the Operations & Admin Support and front desk teams.
  • Liaising with speakers, trainers, and mentors.
  • Supporting scheduling and briefing processes.
  • Assisting with logistics on programme days.

Data and Reporting

Accurate programme data will be an important part of the position.

The Programs Assistant will:

  • Record attendance information.
  • Record participant feedback.
  • Update participant data.
  • Ensure programme data is entered within the same week as each session.
  • Maintain the programme tracker.
  • Identify and flag delays against the delivery calendar.
  • Draft short session reports.
  • Collect participant and stakeholder quotes.
  • Collect photographs.
  • Gather case study material.
  • Share relevant content with the Community & Marketing Assistant for publication.

This means the role combines programme coordination with administrative, reporting, and communication responsibilities.

Community Engagement and Follow-Up

The Programs Assistant will also support ongoing relationships with the entrepreneurship community.

Responsibilities include:

  • Maintaining the mentor database.
  • Maintaining expert contact information.
  • Maintaining facilitator records.
  • Following up with founders.
  • Tracking actions agreed during programmes.
  • Following up on deadlines.
  • Following up on submissions between programme sessions.

Qualifications and Experience

Applicants should have:

  • A degree in business, economics, development studies, social sciences, communications, or a related field.
  • Eligibility for the 2026/2027 national service cycle.
  • Strong written English.
  • The ability to write clear emails.
  • The ability to prepare concise reports without extensive editing.
  • Strong organizational skills.
  • The ability to work toward deadlines.
  • The ability to manage details across several activities at the same time.
  • Confidence when interacting with founders, facilitators, and senior guests.
  • Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills.
  • Willingness to learn Airtable.
  • A genuine interest in entrepreneurship and Ghana’s startup ecosystem.

APPLY HERE

3. National Service Position: Community & Marketing Assistant

Location: Accra, Ghana

Application Deadline: Rolling basis

The Community & Marketing Assistant combines front-of-house, community engagement, content creation, social media, digital communications, and event support responsibilities.

The position is particularly relevant for candidates interested in communications, marketing, journalism, digital content, social media management, photography, videography, hospitality, and community engagement.

The successful candidate will serve as an important point of contact for members, visitors, prospective clients, founders, and other stakeholders visiting the Westerwelle Startup Haus Accra.

The role will also involve transforming activities at the Haus into content for social media, newsletters, websites, and other communication channels.

Key Responsibilities

Front-of-House and Member Support

The Community & Marketing Assistant will help maintain a professional and welcoming environment at the Haus.

Responsibilities include:

  • Opening and closing reception.
  • Ensuring the reception area remains presentable.
  • Maintaining the appearance of the lobby and common areas.
  • Welcoming visitors.
  • Registering visitors.
  • Issuing visitor passes.
  • Directing guests to their hosts.
  • Answering the main telephone line.
  • Monitoring the general enquiries inbox.
  • Responding to enquiries where appropriate.
  • Escalating enquiries when necessary.
  • Checking in members and day-pass users.
  • Maintaining accurate daily occupancy records.
  • Managing meeting room bookings.
  • Managing boardroom bookings.
  • Managing call booth bookings.
  • Resolving scheduling conflicts.
  • Providing campus tours to prospective members.
  • Handing serious membership or business enquiries to the appropriate colleague on the same day.
  • Maintaining the member directory.
  • Maintaining access records in Airtable.

Content Creation and Social Media

A major component of this position is content creation and digital communications.

The successful candidate will:

  • Photograph Haus events.
  • Film programme sessions.
  • Capture community activities and moments.
  • Edit short-form videos.
  • Edit photographs and other visual assets.
  • Draft social media captions.
  • Prepare event recaps.
  • Write short articles.
  • Follow the communication tone of WSHAC.
  • Schedule social media content.
  • Publish content across WSHAC’s social media channels.
  • Follow the established content calendar.
  • Support monthly newsletters.
  • Draft newsletter content.
  • Select suitable images.
  • Maintain newsletter distribution lists.
  • Keep website events pages updated.
  • Keep website news pages updated.
  • Keep team pages current.
  • Maintain an organized media library.
  • Apply appropriate file naming and folder structures.

This makes the opportunity particularly relevant to candidates with practical experience in social media management, photography, videography, graphic design, content creation, digital marketing, or communications.

Brand and Community Engagement

The Community & Marketing Assistant will also contribute to brand consistency and community storytelling.

Responsibilities include:

  • Applying Westerwelle Foundation brand guidelines to content and communication materials.
  • Monitoring social media engagement.
  • Preparing simple monthly performance figures.
  • Collecting founder stories.
  • Collecting member stories.
  • Developing stories that can support reporting.
  • Identifying content that can be used for marketing.
  • Collecting stories that may contribute to fundraising communications.

Event Support

The position also involves supporting events held at the Haus.

Responsibilities include:

  • Supporting registration.
  • Managing guest check-in.
  • Assisting with event signage.
  • Supporting wayfinding.
  • Helping with guest handling during events.
  • Supporting other event-day requirements.

Qualifications and Experience

Applicants for the Community & Marketing Assistant position should have:

  • A Bachelor’s degree or HND in communications, marketing, journalism, hospitality, business administration, or a related discipline.
  • Eligibility for the 2026/2027 national service cycle.
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • A warm, confident, and professional approach to visitors and community members.
  • Strong organizational skills.
  • Reliability and attention to detail.
  • The ability to maintain accurate records.
  • Competence with a camera, including the use of a good smartphone camera.
  • Experience with at least one editing tool such as Canva, CapCut, or Adobe Creative Suite.
  • Clear spoken and written English.
  • A strong understanding of tone and communication.
  • Twi or another Ghanaian language is an added advantage.
  • Familiarity with Microsoft Office.
  • Willingness to learn Airtable.

What the Westerwelle Startup Haus Offers

The three National Service positions offer candidates the opportunity to work in a growing international entrepreneurship ecosystem.

Successful candidates can expect exposure to:

1. A New Entrepreneurship Hub

National service candidates will have the opportunity to contribute to the development and growth of one of Ghana’s newest entrepreneurship hubs.

This can provide practical experience in building systems, supporting programmes, engaging members, managing operations, and contributing to an emerging innovation ecosystem.

2. International and Purpose-Driven Work

The Westerwelle Foundation operates internationally, creating an environment where candidates can interact with people and organizations connected to entrepreneurship, innovation, digital transformation, and development.

3. Startup and Innovation Ecosystem Exposure

The positions can provide exposure to:

  • Startups
  • Entrepreneurs
  • Investors
  • Corporates
  • Universities
  • Mentors
  • International partners
  • Innovation organizations
  • Entrepreneurship programmes
  • Ecosystem stakeholders

4. Professional Development

The positions provide practical workplace experience across areas such as:

  • Administration
  • Finance
  • Procurement
  • Programme management
  • Community engagement
  • Marketing
  • Communications
  • Content creation
  • Event coordination
  • Entrepreneurship support

5. International Collaboration

Candidates may also gain exposure to the wider Westerwelle Foundation network and opportunities for collaboration involving stakeholders across Africa and Europe.

6. Collaborative Working Environment

The Foundation describes its team culture as being built around:

  • Trust
  • Ownership
  • Creativity
  • Collaboration
  • Impact

APPLY HERE

Who Can Apply?

These opportunities are specifically targeted at eligible national service candidates for the 2026/2027 cycle.

The required academic background depends on the position.

Operations & Admin Assistant

Applicants should have a Bachelor’s degree or HND in:

  • Accounting

item.content:encoded:
The King’s Commonwealth Fellowship Programme (KCFP) Undergraduate Fellowships 2027 offer a major opportunity for talented students from eligible Commonwealth Small Island Developing States (SIDS) to pursue undergraduate degrees in their home country or immediate region.

The programme is designed to strengthen local skills, professional capacity and leadership in countries that face significant development challenges, including the growing effects of climate change. Through financial support, professional development and access to an alumni network, the fellowship seeks to equip young people with the knowledge and skills needed to contribute to the long-term development and resilience of their communities.

The 2027 undergraduate fellowship pathway supports students in selected fields including education, engineering, health, environmental health, public health, mathematics education, nursing, sustainable tourism, travel and tourism management, occupational safety and health, geomatics, town and country planning and related disciplines.

Applications opened on 14 September 2026 and will close on 14 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC+1.

About the King’s Commonwealth Fellowship Programme

Commonwealth Small Island Developing States are particularly exposed to climate-related challenges and face increasing demand for qualified professionals in sectors that are important for national development.

The KCFP Undergraduate Fellowships respond to this need by supporting talented students to study at approved KCFP Host Universities located in their home country or, where no approved host university exists in their home country, within their immediate region.

Rather than requiring students to relocate to distant countries for their undergraduate education, the programme is structured around developing skills and expertise within participating island communities.

The programme particularly seeks to contribute to:

  • Strengthening local professional capacity.
  • Addressing medium-term skills shortages.
  • Improving essential services.
  • Supporting sustainable development.
  • Building community resilience.
  • Developing future professionals and leaders.
  • Creating opportunities for young people to contribute to the long-term prosperity of their countries.

The programme also recognises the importance of developing professionals in areas such as education, engineering, health and sustainable tourism.

What Does the KCFP Undergraduate Fellowship Cover?

Successful fellows receive a package of financial support designed to reduce the major costs associated with undergraduate study.

The fellowship provides:

1. Full Tuition Fees

The programme covers full tuition fees where full tuition fees are not already covered by the government. This can substantially reduce the financial burden associated with completing an undergraduate degree.

2. Stipend for Basic Living Costs

Fellows receive a stipend to cover basic living costs during their studies.

This support is intended to help students meet essential day-to-day expenses while undertaking their undergraduate programme.

3. Return Travel to the Home Island

Where applicable, fellows receive one return ticket to their home island for every year of study.

This provision is particularly relevant to students undertaking their studies outside their home island but within the approved regional arrangement.

4. Professional Development and Alumni Network

Beyond financial assistance, the programme is designed to provide fellows with professional development opportunities and access to a strong alumni network.

This broader support is intended to help fellows develop careers that serve their communities and contribute to sustainable national development.

Who Can Apply for the KCFP Undergraduate Fellowship?

The eligibility requirements are specific. Applicants must satisfy all of the conditions established by the programme.

To qualify, an applicant must:

  • Hold citizenship or recognised refugee status in one of the eligible Commonwealth Small Island Developing States.
  • Be due to commence undergraduate study between January and December 2027.
  • Not already hold a higher education qualification, including a bachelor’s degree or postgraduate qualification.
  • Select an undergraduate programme from the approved programmes available at the applicant’s chosen KCFP Host University.
  • Undertake the programme at an approved KCFP Host University in their home country or, where there is no host university in their home country, at an approved university within their immediate region.

Applicants should therefore not assume that any undergraduate course or university will qualify. The programme has published specific host universities and approved undergraduate programmes, and applications for programmes outside the published list will not be considered.

Eligible Commonwealth Small Island Developing States

The fellowship is specifically intended for applicants from 24 eligible Commonwealth Small Island Developing States across the Caribbean and Americas, Indian Ocean and Pacific regions.

Caribbean and Americas

Eligible countries listed by the programme are:

  • Antigua and Barbuda
  • Bahamas
  • Barbados
  • Belize
  • Dominica
  • Grenada
  • Guyana
  • Jamaica
  • St Kitts and Nevis
  • St Lucia
  • St Vincent and the Grenadines
  • Trinidad and Tobago

Indian Ocean

The eligible Indian Ocean SIDS are:

  • Maldives
  • Mauritius
  • Seychelles

Pacific

The eligible Pacific SIDS are:

  • Fiji
  • Kiribati
  • Nauru
  • Papua New Guinea
  • Samoa
  • Solomon Islands
  • Tonga
  • Tuvalu
  • Vanuatu

The programme’s eligibility requirements expressly refer to citizenship or refugee status in these Commonwealth SIDS.

Approved Host Universities and Undergraduate Programmes

One of the most important features of the KCFP Undergraduate Fellowship is that applicants must choose from the approved programmes at participating host universities.

The available programmes cover a range of disciplines connected to national development, health, education, engineering, environmental sustainability and tourism.

Fiji National University

Approved programmes include:

  • Bachelor of Environmental Health
  • Bachelor of Public Health
  • Bachelor of Education (Secondary) (Mathematics & Physics) – Mathematics Specialisation
  • Bachelor of Education (Secondary) (Mathematics & Physics) – Physics Specialisation
  • Bachelor of Education (Primary) – Primary School Teaching Specialist

Applicants from Fiji, Kiribati, Nauru, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu may be considered for the listed programmes at Fiji National University.

National University of Samoa

Available undergraduate programmes include:

  • Bachelor of Education (Primary)
  • Bachelor of Nursing
  • Bachelor of Health Sciences
  • Bachelor of Science (Secondary Teaching)

The listed eligible applicants are from Kiribati, Nauru, Samoa, Tonga, Tuvalu and Vanuatu.

Papua New Guinea University of Technology

The approved programmes include:

  • Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering (Honours)
  • Bachelor of Electrical Engineering (Honours)
  • Bachelor of Civil Engineering (Honours)

Applicants from Papua New Guinea and Solomon Islands are listed for these programmes.

University of Belize

The available programmes are:

  • Bachelor in Nursing
  • Bachelor in Mathematics Education

Applicants from Bahamas, Belize and Jamaica are listed for these programmes.

University of Mauritius

The approved programmes include:

  • BEng (Hons) Civil Engineering
  • BSc (Hons) Geomatics
  • BSc (Hons) Town and Country Planning

The listed applicants are from Mauritius and Seychelles.

University of Technology, Mauritius

Students can apply for:

  • BSc (Hons) Occupational Safety and Health Management
  • BSc (Hons) Travel and Tourism Management

The programme lists Mauritius and Seychelles as the eligible applicant countries for these programmes.

University of the West Indies, Cave Hill

The approved programme is:

  • Bachelor of Health Sciences

Applicants listed for this programme are from Antigua and Barbuda, Barbados, Dominica, Grenada, Guyana, Jamaica, St Kitts and Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines, and Trinidad and Tobago.

Villa College

Approved programmes include:

  • Bachelor of Nursing
  • Bachelor of Teaching in Primary and Special Educational Needs
  • Bachelor of Mechanical Engineering (Honours)
  • Bachelor of Electrical and Electronics Engineering (Honours)
  • Bachelor of Civil Engineering (Honours)

The listed eligible applicants are from Maldives.

How the Host University Arrangement Works

The fellowship is designed to allow applicants to undertake their undergraduate studies as close as possible to their home communities.

Applicants are expected to study at an approved KCFP Host University located in their home country.

If an applicant’s home country does not have an approved host university, the applicant may study at another approved KCFP Host University located within their immediate region.

This regional approach allows the programme to provide access to approved higher education opportunities while maintaining a strong connection between fellows and their island communities.

Applicants should consult the programme’s official application guidance because admission requirements can differ according to the undergraduate programme and host university.

How Many Fellowships Are Available?

A total of 11 King’s Commonwealth Fellowships are available through this undergraduate pathway.

The fellowships are divided into two groups:

  • Seven fellowships are ringfenced for applicants who are citizens of, or hold recognised refugee status in, seven specified SIDS.
  • Four fellowships are open to applicants from all 24 eligible Commonwealth Small Island Developing States.

The seven countries with ringfenced fellowships are:

  • Dominica
  • Grenada
  • Kiribati
  • Nauru
  • Samoa
  • Tonga
  • Tuvalu

Applicants from these seven countries will be considered for both the ringfenced fellowships and the wider open competition, provided that they meet all other eligibility requirements.

Encouragement for Indigenous Communities

The programme states that people belonging to indigenous communities are especially encouraged to apply.

However, belonging to an indigenous community is not an eligibility requirement. Applicants who do not belong to an indigenous community can still be eligible if they satisfy the programme’s other requirements.

When Will the Fellowship Take Place?

Successful applicants are expected to commence their undergraduate studies between January and December 2027.

This means prospective applicants should make sure that their selected programme and expected admission timeline align with the 2027 commencement requirement.

Application Deadline

The King’s Commonwealth Fellowship Programme Undergraduate Fellowship application deadline is 14 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC+1.

Applications opened on 14 September 2026.

Applicants should not wait until the final hours to submit their applications. The ACU specifically advises prospective applicants to read the application guidance and frequently asked questions carefully before beginning the application.

How to Apply

Interested applicants should first establish that they meet all eligibility requirements and that their preferred undergraduate programme appears on the approved programme list.

The recommended process is:

  1. Check your country eligibility.
    Confirm that you are a citizen or recognised refugee in one of the 24 eligible Commonwealth SIDS.
  2. Confirm your undergraduate status.
    Applicants must be preparing to commence undergraduate study between January and December 2027 and must not already hold a higher education qualification.
  3. Review the approved programmes.
    Make sure your intended degree is among the programmes approved under the KCFP Undergraduate Fellowship pathway.
  4. Check the appropriate host university.
    Determine which KCFP Host University and programme correspond to your country.
  5. Review admission requirements.
    The programme notes that admission requirements for individual undergraduate programmes are provided in the official application guidance.
  6. Read the application guidance and FAQs.
    The ACU strongly recommends that applicants familiarise themselves with these documents before starting the application.
  7. Submit the application before the deadline.
    Applications must be submitted by 14 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC+1.

The official application page is provided by the Association of Commonwealth Universities.

Click HERE to Apply

Important Considerations Before Applying

The KCFP Undergraduate Fellowship is not an unrestricted undergraduate scholarship. There are several conditions applicants should pay particular attention to.

First, applicants must come from an eligible Commonwealth Small Island Developing State. Second, they must not already hold a higher education qualification. Third, the programme of study must be among the approved undergraduate programmes.

Applicants should therefore avoid selecting a course simply because it is available at one of the participating universities. The course must specifically appear within the KCFP-approved programme list.

Applicants should also verify the admission requirements for their chosen programme because meeting the fellowship eligibility criteria does not necessarily mean that an applicant automatically meets every admission requirement of the host university or degree programme.

Why the Programme Matters

The KCFP Undergraduate Fellowship is structured around a broader development objective rather than undergraduate education alone.

The programme recognises that many Small Island Developing States require additional skilled professionals in areas directly connected to national development and resilience.

By supporting students in fields such as:

  • Education
  • Nursing
  • Public health
  • Environmental health
  • Engineering
  • Mathematics education
  • Geomatics
  • Town and country planning
  • Occupational safety and health
  • Travel and tourism

the programme seeks to contribute to local capacity and help participating countries respond to long-term development needs.

The fellowship therefore combines educational opportunity with an emphasis on developing professionals who can contribute to their communities after completing their studies.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the KCFP Undergraduate Fellowship fully funded?

The programme provides full tuition fees where full tuition fees are not covered by the government, a stipend for basic living costs and, where applicable, one return ticket to the home island for every year of study.

Who is eligible?

The fellowship is for eligible citizens or recognised refugees from 24 Commonwealth Small Island Developing States who satisfy the programme’s undergraduate study, qualification and approved-programme requirements.

Can someone who already has a bachelor’s degree apply?

No. The programme states that applicants must not hold a higher education qualification, including a bachelor’s degree or postgraduate qualification.

When must successful applicants begin their undergraduate studies?

Applicants must be due to commence undergraduate study between January and December 2027.

Can applicants choose any university?

No. Applicants must select an approved undergraduate programme at a KCFP Host University. Where there is no approved host university in the applicant’s home country, study may take place at an approved host university within the applicant’s immediate region.

How many fellowships are available?

There are 11 fellowships under this undergraduate pathway: seven ringfenced for applicants from seven specified SIDS and four open to applicants from all 24 eligible Commonwealth SIDS.

Are indigenous applicants required to apply?

No. The programme particularly encourages people from indigenous communities to apply, but indigenous identity is not an eligibility requirement.

What is the application deadline?

The deadline is 14 October 2026 at 15:00 UTC+1.

Learn More HERE

Conclusion

The King’s Commonwealth Fellowship Programme Undergraduate Fellowships 2027 provide an opportunity for eligible students from Commonwealth Small Island Developing States to pursue selected undergraduate degrees while receiving substantial financial support.

With support covering tuition where applicable, a living-cost stipend and return travel where applicable, the programme is designed not only to support individual students but also to strengthen professional capacity in participating island communities.

Because the fellowship is limited to specific countries, approved host universities and approved undergraduate programmes, prospective applicants should carefully check the official eligibility requirements before applying. They should also review the programme-specific admission requirements, application guidance and FAQs well before the deadline.

Eligible applicants who intend to begin an approved undergraduate programme in 2027 should take note of the 14 October 2026, 15:00 UTC+1 deadline and complete their applications in accordance with the official instructions.

Official application: https://crm.acu.ac.uk/form/kcfp-undergraduate-applications

Application guidance and FAQs: Applicants are advised by the ACU to review the Official Guidance and FAQs before beginning their application.

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the University of Sheffield AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award (DLA) for 2027/28 entry, offering four fully funded PhD studentships for doctoral researchers undertaking eligible projects within the University’s Faculty of Arts and Humanities.

The programme is supported through the Arts and Humanities Research Council (AHRC) and forms part of the AHRC North/Northwest Hub, connecting Sheffield’s doctoral researchers with a wider regional network of universities and postgraduate researchers.

The award is particularly significant because it is not restricted to traditionally defined arts and humanities disciplines. Eligible applicants may pursue doctoral research through four Sheffield schools, including the School of Law, opening the competition to suitable legal research projects alongside work in English, history, philosophy, digital humanities, languages, arts and societies.

Each studentship provides 3.5 years of funding for full-time study, with funding provided pro rata for part-time candidates. The package consists of a maintenance stipend at the UKRI rate — currently £21,805 for the 2026/27 academic year — plus payment of tuition fees at the applicable Home or International rate.

International applicants are welcome. However, candidates applying from overseas should note an important limitation: up to one of the four annual studentships may be allocated to an outstanding international candidate, making the international competition particularly selective.

Applicants must also pay close attention to the programme’s two-stage application process and two separate deadlines. Candidates first need to submit an application for a PhD place at the University of Sheffield by 14 December 2026. After obtaining their University study application number, they must separately submit the AHRC DLA funding application by 5:00 PM GMT on 19 February 2027.

Importantly, the published instructions require candidates to submit their PhD application first and obtain an application number before completing the funding form. They do not state that applicants must wait until they have received a formal PhD offer before submitting the scholarship application.

The scheme is not open to candidates who are already enrolled on a PhD.

Official AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award page at the University of Sheffield

About the AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award at the University of Sheffield

The AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award, commonly abbreviated to DLA, supports postgraduate researchers working across the arts and humanities.

The University of Sheffield has received a Doctoral Landscape Award to support doctoral researchers within its Faculty of Arts and Humanities.

Sheffield’s studentships are associated with the AHRC North/Northwest Hub, in collaboration with nine other universities in the region.

The structure is intended to provide doctoral researchers with more than individual supervision and financial support. Successful candidates become members of a broader doctoral cohort and are expected to participate actively in:

  • Cohort training
  • Professional development
  • Research activities
  • Interdisciplinary engagement
  • Other activities organized through the DLA North/Northwest Hub

Recipients should therefore view the studentship as both PhD funding and participation in a wider doctoral training community.

How Many AHRC DLA Studentships Are Available?

The University of Sheffield will support:

Four full PhD studentships per year.

This means that the funding competition is likely to be highly selective.

The four awards are available across the Faculty of Arts and Humanities rather than being separately guaranteed to each School.

Applicants will initially be assessed within the relevant academic School before shortlisted candidates progress to the Faculty-level selection process.

Which University of Sheffield Schools Are Included?

The Faculty of Arts and Humanities includes four participating academic Schools:

School of English

Research undertaken through the School of English may fall within fields such as literature, language, creative writing and related interdisciplinary areas, depending on available supervision and PhD admission requirements.

School of History, Philosophy and Digital Humanities

This School brings together doctoral research across historical, philosophical and digital-humanities approaches.

School of Languages, Arts and Societies

Researchers working across languages, cultures, societies and arts-related fields may be based within this School.

School of Law

Importantly, the School of Law is explicitly included in the Faculty for the purposes of this DLA competition.

This means candidates pursuing qualifying arts-and-humanities-oriented doctoral research in law may also apply, subject to obtaining admission to an appropriate Sheffield PhD programme and meeting the funding competition requirements.

The inclusion of Law makes this opportunity particularly relevant to prospective PhD researchers working on areas such as legal history, jurisprudence, socio-legal research and other projects that fit the AHRC and Faculty research environment.

A Large Arts, Humanities and Law Research Community

The University states that the Faculty is home to more than 200 PhD researchers undertaking disciplinary and interdisciplinary research.

It also has more than two dozen Faculty Research Centres bringing together:

  • Academic staff
  • Postgraduate researchers
  • Early-career researchers
  • Regional stakeholders

This research-centre structure is especially important for applicants because the DLA funding application asks candidates to explain how their proposed research will align not only with their prospective supervisor and School, but also with one or more of the Faculty’s research centres.

Candidates should therefore research Sheffield’s institutional environment carefully before submitting their application.

Simply demonstrating that a supervisor works on a similar topic may not be sufficient for a strong funding application. Applicants are expected to show how their project fits into the wider intellectual environment available at Sheffield.

AHRC DLA Funding Package

The studentships are funded for:

3.5 years for full-time study

with funding adjusted pro rata for part-time study.

The award consists of two major components.

1. UKRI Maintenance Stipend

Successful candidates will receive a maintenance stipend at the UKRI rate.

The University currently lists the stipend as:

£21,805 for the 2026/27 academic year.

Candidates entering in 2027/28 should understand that this is the current published rate, rather than assume £21,805 will necessarily remain the exact figure throughout their award.

UKRI stipend rates can change between academic years.

The maintenance stipend is intended to help doctoral researchers meet living expenses while completing their PhD.

2. Tuition Fee Funding

The studentship also includes payment of:

Tuition fees at the applicable Home or International rate.

This is particularly important for international candidates because overseas PhD tuition fees can be substantially higher than Home fees.

The University explicitly states that the award covers:

  • Home tuition fees, where applicable; or
  • International tuition fees, where applicable.

Therefore, an international candidate who receives one of these studentships would have the applicable international tuition fees covered under the award.

Is the AHRC DLA Open to International Students?

Yes.

Overseas students are welcome to apply.

However, international applicants should understand the funding allocation carefully.

The University states that:

Up to one of the four studentships may be allocated to an outstanding international candidate.

This means international candidates are eligible, but the number of awards potentially available to them is more restricted.

The University itself warns that competition for the international place is therefore expected to be particularly intense.

Prospective overseas applicants should not interpret international eligibility as meaning there are four international awards.

There are four studentships overall, and up to one may go to an outstanding international applicant.

Can Current PhD Students Apply?

No.

The University explicitly states:

The scheme is not open to candidates who are already enrolled on a PhD.

This is an important eligibility condition.

The competition is therefore intended for candidates applying to begin a new PhD programme at Sheffield for the relevant entry cycle rather than current Sheffield PhD students seeking funding partway through an existing doctorate.

Two Separate Applications Are Required

One of the most important aspects of the AHRC DLA competition is that applying for PhD admission and applying for funding are two separate processes.

Candidates cannot simply submit the funding form without first applying for doctoral study.

The sequence is:

  1. Submit a University of Sheffield PhD study application.
  2. Receive your University application number.
  3. Submit the separate AHRC DLA funding application using that number.

Applicants should therefore begin preparing much earlier than the February scholarship deadline.

Step 1: Apply for a PhD Place at the University of Sheffield

Candidates must first submit their application for doctoral study through the University of Sheffield’s postgraduate application system.

The deadline for the PhD study application is:

Monday, 14 December 2026.

Submit a University of Sheffield postgraduate research application

This first deadline is extremely important.

A prospective candidate cannot simply wait until February to begin the process because the funding application requires the study-application number generated following submission of the PhD application.

Do You Need a PhD Offer Before Applying for the Scholarship?

The published instructions make an important distinction.

Candidates must submit their PhD study application first, but the funding instructions do not say that they need to wait for a formal offer of admission.

Instead, after submitting the study application, candidates receive an application number.

The DLA funding form asks applicants to enter this number.

The application guidance identifies it as the nine-digit application number assigned following submission of the University study application.

Therefore, the correct sequence is:

PhD application submitted → application number received → DLA funding application submitted.

Applicants should not unnecessarily delay their funding application while waiting for a formal admission decision unless Sheffield separately instructs them to do so.

Step 2: Submit the AHRC DLA Funding Application

Once the doctoral application has been submitted and the candidate has received their study application number, they can complete the separate DLA funding form.

The final deadline for this stage is:

5:00 PM GMT on Friday, 19 February 2027.

AHRC DLA 2027/28 funding application form

The University states that the funding application must be completed in one sitting.

This makes advance preparation especially important.

Use the Application Guidance Template Before Opening the Final Form

The University provides an application guidance template that prospective candidates can use to draft their answers before entering them into the final online form.

The guidance clearly states that it is not itself the application form.

Candidates can use it to prepare responses in advance and then transfer their final answers into the funding form.

AHRC DLA 2027/28 application guidance template

This is particularly useful because several sections have strict word limits.

What Does the AHRC DLA Funding Application Ask For?

The 2027/28 application guidance provides considerably more detail about what candidates need to prepare.

Applicant Details

Applicants are asked to provide basic information including:

  • Forename
  • Surname
  • School to which they have applied
  • Nine-digit PhD application number
  • Email address

Candidates select from the participating Schools:

  • School of English
  • School of History, Philosophy and Digital Humanities
  • School of Languages, Arts and Societies
  • School of Law

Research Project Proposal

The proposed PhD project is central to the funding application.

Candidates must provide:

Prospective supervisor

Applicants should identify the academic they expect to supervise their doctoral research.

This reinforces the importance of researching potential supervisors before submitting the application.

Project title

A clear title for the proposed PhD research is required.

150-word project summary

Candidates must summarize their proposed doctoral project in:

150 words.

This requires a highly concise explanation of:

  • Research problem
  • Central question
  • Approach
  • Contribution

Applicants should not treat this section as simply an abbreviated literature review.

Its purpose is to communicate the research project clearly and quickly.

Detailed Research Proposal: 500–1,000 Words

The DLA application also requires a detailed project proposal of:

500–1,000 words, excluding references.

The guidance states that this should match the proposal submitted with the candidate’s application for a PhD place.

The proposal must address:

  • The questions or hypotheses the research will examine
  • The research methods that will be used
  • The sources or datasets that will be consulted
  • How the project relates to existing research within the discipline
  • The contribution the research is expected to make to the discipline

Candidates should respect the word limit carefully.

The guidance explicitly warns that the DLA reserves the right to reject responses that are excessively long.

Demonstrating Fit With Sheffield

Candidates are also asked to explain in detail how their project aligns with:

  • The expertise of their proposed supervisor or supervisors
  • The research culture of the relevant School
  • One or more Faculty Research Centres

This is an important part of the competition.

A funding proposal should therefore not read like a generic PhD application that could be submitted to any university.

Applicants should demonstrate why Sheffield specifically is an appropriate intellectual environment for the project.

This may include identifying:

  • Relevant academics
  • Research groups
  • Faculty centres
  • Methodological expertise
  • Interdisciplinary networks
  • Archives or other research resources

Fieldwork and Archival Research

The form asks applicants to describe any:

  • Fieldwork
  • Archival visits

that will be required for the proposed project.

Candidates should therefore think through the practical design of their PhD rather than describing only an abstract research question.

Where relevant, this section can help demonstrate that the project is feasible within the funded period.

Partner Organizations

Applicants may also provide details of external partner organizations that will have direct involvement in their research.

Examples identified by the guidance include:

  • Heritage organizations
  • Cultural organizations
  • Policy organizations

The form asks candidates to explain what role the organization will play, such as:

  • Co-supervision
  • Exhibition opportunities
  • Public engagement
  • Other direct research involvement

Organizations that merely provide access to datasets or research materials do not need to be listed in this section.

Academic Qualifications

Applicants can enter up to three qualifications already completed.

These might include:

  • Bachelor’s or equivalent undergraduate degree
  • Master’s or equivalent postgraduate degree
  • Another university or professional qualification relevant to the project

For each qualification, applicants are asked for information such as:

  • Institution
  • Country
  • Type of qualification
  • Programme title
  • Completion date
  • Classification, grade or GPA

The DLA page itself does not state one universal minimum GPA or degree classification for all applicants.

Candidates must therefore also satisfy the admission requirements for the specific Sheffield PhD programme and School to which they are applying.

Qualification Currently in Progress

Candidates who are still completing a qualification can provide details of one qualification currently in progress.

The form asks for:

  • Institution and country
  • Qualification type
  • Programme title
  • Expected completion date

This is relevant for applicants currently completing, for example, a Master’s degree before beginning doctoral study.

Relevant Work Experience

Work experience is an optional section.

Applicants can provide up to:

Three relevant work experiences.

The University asks candidates to include only employment that is directly relevant to the funding application.

For each role, applicants may provide:

  • Employer
  • Job title
  • Description of responsibilities
  • Start date
  • End date, where applicable

The fact that this section is optional is important: lack of formal professional experience does not automatically make someone ineligible.

Publications

Publications are also optional.

Candidates can list up to:

Five publications.

Eligible examples include:

  • Academic papers
  • Conference proceedings
  • Professional reports
  • Book chapters
  • Books

Papers that have been formally accepted but are not yet published may be listed.

However, applicants should not include work that has not yet been accepted for publication.

The application guidance also explicitly reassures candidates not to worry if they have no publications, recognizing that publishing expectations differ considerably between academic disciplines.

This means applicants should not assume that an extensive publication record is mandatory.

Performances, Compositions, Exhibitions and Presentations

The application includes another optional section that is particularly relevant to:

  • Creative-practice researchers
  • Applicants with artistic outputs
  • Candidates who have given research presentations
  • Candidates with professional-practice presentations

Applicants can provide up to:

Five relevant activities.

Examples may include:

  • Performances
  • Compositions
  • Exhibitions
  • Presentations

Candidates can describe their own contribution and, where appropriate, provide quantitative evidence such as:

  • Visitor numbers
  • Listener figures
  • Views
  • Reviews
  • Awards

This reflects the breadth of arts and humanities research and recognizes research excellence beyond conventional journal publications.

Competitive Prizes and Awards

Applicants may list up to:

Two competitive prizes or awards.

The guidance asks candidates to include only awards that were competitively awarded and relevant to demonstrating qualities connected to the application.

Examples might relate to:

  • Essay writing
  • Dissertation work
  • Performance
  • Research presentations
  • Professional practice

Candidates are also asked to identify whether an award was:

  • Departmental
  • Institutional
  • Regional
  • National
  • International

This section is optional.

Selection Process

Once the funding deadline passes, applications move through several stages.

First Stage: School-Level Assessment

Applications are shared with the relevant School for the first phase of assessment.

This means applicants are initially considered in relation to the academic environment in which their proposed PhD would be based.

Second Stage: Faculty Nomination

Candidates selected by their School are nominated to a Faculty panel.

Faculty Panel: March 2027

The Faculty selection panel is expected to convene in:

March 2027.

The panel will confirm the final studentship selections.

Final Results

The University aims to notify all applicants of the final outcome by:

The end of March 2027.

Candidates should therefore expect the full scholarship decision process to continue for several weeks following the February funding deadline.

DLA Cohort Participation

Successful candidates do not simply receive funding and work independently with their supervisors.

Recipients will become part of the:

DLA North/North West Hub cohort

and are expected to participate fully in:

  • Cohort training
  • Development activities
  • Other Hub programming

Applicants should therefore be interested in contributing to a broader doctoral community alongside completing their individual research.

Part-Time Applicants

The University describes the 3.5-year studentships as being funded pro rata for part-time study.

This indicates that part-time doctoral study can be accommodated under the funding structure, subject to the relevant University arrangements and programme requirements.

Applicants considering this route should confirm the precise funding duration and study arrangements with Sheffield.

Important Deadlines

Prospective applicants should keep both deadlines clearly separated:

PhD study application deadline:
Monday, 14 December 2026

AHRC DLA funding application deadline:
Friday, 19 February 2027 at 5:00 PM GMT

Missing the December study deadline may prevent a candidate from obtaining the application number required for the funding competition.

The February date should therefore never be treated as the only deadline for this opportunity.

How to Prepare a Strong Application

Because only four studentships are available, candidates should prepare both their PhD application and funding application carefully.

1. Identify the Right Supervisor Early

Your proposal must fit the expertise of your prospective supervisor.

Candidates should investigate:

  • Academic research profiles
  • Recent publications
  • Research interests
  • Relevant research centres

before finalizing their project.

2. Demonstrate Institutional Fit

Do not merely explain why your research topic is important.

Explain why the project belongs at Sheffield.

Connect your proposal directly to:

  • Supervisor expertise
  • School research strengths
  • Faculty Research Centres

3. Make the Research Question Precise

A competitive proposal should identify a researchable question rather than simply naming a broad subject.

For example, “international human rights law” is a field.

A strong PhD proposal would instead identify a specific legal problem, body of evidence, theoretical debate and potential contribution.

4. Explain the Contribution

The funding form explicitly asks what contribution the research will make to the discipline.

Candidates should therefore distinguish clearly between:

  • What previous scholarship has established
  • What remains unresolved
  • How their research will address that gap
  • Why that contribution matters

5. Take Methodology Seriously

The application asks candidates to explain their research methods.

The methodology should be directly connected to the research question rather than included as a generic list of techniques.

6. Respect Every Word Limit

The project summary is limited to 150 words, while the detailed proposal is 500–1,000 words excluding references.

The guidance warns that overly long responses may be rejected.

7. Draft Before Opening the Funding Form

Because the final funding application must be submitted in one sitting, prepare and proofread all answers in advance using the University’s guidance template.

Key Details at a Glance

Programme: AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award 2027/28

University: University of Sheffield

Country: United Kingdom

Level: PhD

Number of studentships: Four per year

Duration: 3.5 years full-time, pro rata for part-time

Maintenance funding: UKRI stipend rate, currently £21,805 for 2026/27

Tuition: Home or International fees covered as applicable

International eligibility: Yes

International award limit: Up to one of the four studentships may be awarded to an outstanding international candidate

Current PhD students: Not eligible

Eligible Faculty: Faculty of Arts and Humanities

Participating Schools: English; History, Philosophy and Digital Humanities; Languages, Arts and Societies; Law

PhD application deadline: 14 December 2026

Funding deadline: 19 February 2027 at 5:00 PM GMT

Faculty selection: March 2027

Expected final notification: By the end of March 2027

Official information:
University of Sheffield AHRC DLA page

Conclusion

The University of Sheffield AHRC Doctoral Landscape Award 2027/28 offers a substantial funding opportunity for prospective researchers seeking to undertake doctoral study across arts, humanities and qualifying Law research at Sheffield.

Four studentships are available each year. Each provides 3.5 years of support for full-time study, with pro-rata arrangements for part-time candidates, and includes both a UKRI-rate maintenance stipend and tuition-fee coverage.

The current published UKRI stipend is £21,805 for the 2026/27 academic year, although the applicable rate may change for the 2027/28 entry year.

International candidates can apply and, importantly, international tuition fees are covered for a successful overseas award holder. However, overseas applicants should recognize the particularly competitive structure: up to one of the four studentships may be allocated to an international candidate.

Candidates also need to plan ahead because there are two application stages. The PhD study application must be submitted by 14 December 2026, while the separate DLA funding application closes at 5:00 PM GMT on 19 February 2027.

Applicants do not need to wait until February to begin preparing their scholarship materials. The University provides a detailed guidance template covering the research summary, 500–1,000-word proposal, supervisory and institutional fit, qualifications, relevant experience, publications and other achievements.

For prospective doctoral researchers, especially those interested in the School of Law as well as Sheffield’s broader arts and humanities disciplines, the strongest applications will combine a clearly defined original project with a compelling explanation of why Sheffield’s supervisors, research culture and research centres provide the right environment in which to undertake it.

item.content:encoded:
The MOPGA 2027 Visiting Fellowship Program for Early-Career Researchers offers international researchers an opportunity to undertake a 12-month research stay in France and contribute to research addressing some of the world’s most pressing climate change and environmental challenges.

The program, known as Make Our Planet Great Again (MOPGA), is part of France’s broader efforts to strengthen international scientific cooperation around climate change and environmental issues. The 2027 call is designed specifically for early-career researchers who have recently completed their doctoral studies and wish to pursue international research mobility in France.

Successful applicants will undertake their research projects in collaboration with French research institutions, creating opportunities for international scientific exchange and collaboration.

The application deadline for the MOPGA 2027 fellowship is December 15, 2026.

What Is the MOPGA 2027 Visiting Fellowship Program?

The MOPGA 2027 Visiting Fellowship Program is a research fellowship initiative for early-career international researchers who want to conduct research in France on climate change and environmental topics.

The initiative is connected to France’s commitment to addressing climate change and supporting the objectives associated with the Paris Agreement. It seeks to strengthen scientific contributions to climate-related challenges discussed through the international climate process, including the Conferences of the Parties (COP).

Through the program, researchers from outside France can undertake a research stay at a French research institution, allowing them to develop their research while collaborating with researchers and institutions in France.

The 2027 fellowship will support successful researchers for a period of 12 months, with research stays scheduled to begin in September 2027.

MOPGA 2027 Fellowship at a Glance

Opportunity Details
Program MOPGA 2027 Visiting Fellowship Program
Full name Make Our Planet Great Again
Host country France
Opportunity type Visiting research fellowship
Target group Early-career international researchers
Research focus Climate change and environmental topics
Fellowship duration 12 months
Start date September 2027
Application deadline December 15, 2026
Nationality requirement Foreign nationality; French nationals are not eligible
Doctoral requirement PhD awarded less than five years before the deadline
Application purpose International research mobility to France
Implementation Campus France
Funding institutions Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs (MEAE), in partnership with the Ministry of Higher Education, Research and Space (MESRE)

What Does the MOPGA 2027 Fellowship Aim to Achieve?

Climate change requires scientific research that crosses national and disciplinary boundaries. The MOPGA program is intended to contribute to this international research effort by encouraging researchers from around the world to conduct research in France.

The program has several interconnected objectives.

1. Strengthening Climate Change Research

One of the central purposes of the fellowship is to support research addressing climate change and environmental challenges.

Researchers whose work contributes to understanding or addressing these issues can use the fellowship as an opportunity to pursue their research within the French research environment.

2. Promoting International Scientific Mobility

The program is specifically designed around international mobility.

Successful applicants will travel to France to undertake their research rather than simply conducting the project from their home country. This international mobility can facilitate interaction between researchers, institutions, laboratories, and academic networks.

3. Supporting Collaboration With French Research Institutions

MOPGA 2027 will allow successful researchers to develop their projects in collaboration with leading French research institutions.

This creates an environment in which international researchers can engage with French academic and scientific expertise while advancing their own research projects.

4. Contributing to International Climate Goals

The fellowship is linked to France’s role in international efforts to address climate change and its commitment to the spirit of the Paris Agreement.

The program therefore places scientific research within a broader international effort to understand and respond to environmental and climate challenges.

Who Is Eligible for the MOPGA 2027 Fellowship?

The MOPGA 2027 program is specifically aimed at early-career international researchers.

Applicants must satisfy several eligibility requirements.

1. Applicants Must Hold a Doctoral Degree

Applicants must have a doctoral degree.

Importantly, the PhD must have been awarded less than five years before the application deadline.

For the 2027 call, applicants must therefore have defended their doctoral thesis between:

December 2021 and December 2026, inclusive.

This means the program is specifically targeted toward researchers who are relatively early in their postdoctoral careers.

2. Applicants Must Be Foreign Nationals

The fellowship is intended for international researchers who are not French nationals.

The eligibility rules specify that applicants must be exclusively of foreign nationality.

The program is therefore open to researchers from different countries around the world, provided they meet the other eligibility requirements.

French nationals are not eligible.

3. Applicants Must Undertake Research Mobility to France

Applicants must apply with the purpose of undertaking international research mobility in France.

The program is not designed simply to provide funding for researchers to remain in their home countries.

Successful candidates are expected to conduct their research stay in France and collaborate with French research institutions.

4. Applicants Must Not Be Living and Professionally Active in France

At the time of application, candidates must not be residing and professionally active in France.

This requirement is important because the fellowship is intended to facilitate international mobility into the French research environment.

Researchers already living and professionally active in France at the time they apply do not meet this particular eligibility condition.

5. Previous MOPGA Fellows Are Not Eligible

Applicants must not have previously received a MOPGA fellowship.

The program is therefore intended to support researchers who have not already benefited from this particular fellowship scheme.

What Research Areas Does MOPGA 2027 Support?

The 2027 MOPGA call is focused on climate change and environmental topics.

This makes the fellowship particularly relevant to researchers whose doctoral or postdoctoral research relates to environmental and climate-related questions.

The program description emphasizes the importance of scientific contributions to the climate change issues raised through the international Conferences of the Parties.

Researchers should consult the official MOPGA 2027 call for the detailed list of eligible research topics and application requirements before preparing their proposal.

Read the official MOPGA 2027 call for applications

How Long Is the MOPGA Fellowship?

Successful researchers will receive support for a 12-month research stay.

The fellowship period is scheduled to begin in:

September 2027

A full year of research in France can provide an opportunity for fellows to develop their research projects, collaborate with French institutions, and participate in the country’s scientific research environment.

Why Is the MOPGA 2027 Fellowship Important for Early-Career Researchers?

For researchers who have recently completed their PhDs, establishing international research connections can be an important part of developing an academic or scientific career.

The MOPGA fellowship is structured around international mobility and research collaboration, making it relevant to researchers who want to expand their professional and academic networks beyond their home institutions.

Potential areas of value include:

  • Conducting research in France for 12 months
  • Developing international research experience
  • Collaborating with French research institutions
  • Building connections with researchers in France
  • Advancing a research project related to climate change or environmental issues
  • Participating in international scientific collaboration
  • Developing experience in a new academic and research environment
  • Connecting research with broader international climate-change priorities

The precise financial provisions and conditions of the fellowship should be reviewed in the official 2027 call before applicants make plans based on the funding.

France as a Destination for International Research

France has an extensive higher education and research ecosystem, including universities, laboratories, research institutes, and other scientific institutions.

The MOPGA program uses this research environment to encourage international researchers to collaborate with French institutions.

For early-career researchers, spending a year conducting research in another country’s academic environment can also provide exposure to different research networks, methodologies, institutional practices, and potential future collaborations.

Who Can Benefit From Applying?

The fellowship is particularly relevant to researchers who:

  • Have recently completed a PhD
  • Are working on climate change research
  • Conduct research related to environmental issues
  • Want to undertake research in France
  • Are seeking international research experience
  • Want to collaborate with French research institutions
  • Are interested in international scientific cooperation
  • Have not previously received a MOPGA fellowship
  • Are currently outside France and not professionally active there
  • Meet the nationality and doctoral-degree requirements

Applicants should carefully compare their research profile with the official call before beginning the application.

Important Eligibility Conditions to Check Before Applying

Because the MOPGA 2027 fellowship has specific eligibility requirements, prospective applicants should verify each of the following points:

Academic eligibility

You must hold a doctoral degree, and your thesis must have been defended between December 2021 and December 2026.

Nationality

You must be a foreign national. French nationality is excluded.

Mobility

Your application must involve research mobility to France.

Current location and employment

You must not be residing and professionally active in France at the time you apply.

Previous participation

You must not have previously received a MOPGA fellowship.

Research area

Your proposed research must fall within the climate change and environmental focus of the call.

MOPGA 2027 Application Deadline

The application deadline for the MOPGA 2027 Visiting Fellowship Program is:

December 15, 2026

Applicants should not wait until the final day to begin preparing their applications. Research fellowship applications can require time to develop a research proposal, identify an appropriate host institution or research environment, gather academic documents, and complete the required application materials.

Applicants should also carefully check the official call for any additional requirements concerning the research project, host institution, documentation, or submission procedure.
